Figure 5. Analysis of total iterations of memory distillation. The distilled model is trained for the number of iterations indicated on the x-axis. The final model is fine-tuned with data selection with 10, 000 total iterations.

Figure 1. Overview of the three-stage MeDS pipeline. First stage: memory construction. From each training image x ∈ D, a frozen teacher network g extracts patch features g(x)hw ∈ RC for all spatial positions (h,w). The pooled feature collection g(D) ⊆ RC of size |g(D)| = |D| ·H ·W is randomly subsampled B times at ratio ρ to form partial memory banks {Mb}Bb=1. Each memory bank Mb produces a per-patch nearest-neighbor distance score sMb(x) ∈ RH×W , and averaging these scores across all B memory banks yields the ensemble score sM(x) ∈ RH×W . The sparse subsampling acts as a low-pass filter that downweights anomalous patches. Second stage: memory score distillation. For further enhancement, the memory score sM is distilled into a network-based reconstruction score sθ via minθ∥sM(x)−sθ(x)∥2, where sθ(x) ∈ RH×W is the distance between teacher features g(x) and the features fθ(x) ∈ RH×W×C extracted from a student network fθ . Third stage: fine-tuning with progressive selection. Finally, the reconstruction score sθ is fine-tuned on a clean subset St ⊆ D obtained by a progressive selection criterion.
